articles.title: Nessun Dolore review – sketchy Roman fable of liberal white guilt
articles.summary: Venice film festival A white man’s eyes are opened to cruelty and racism when a young boy is thrust into his life in Gianni Amelio’s bold but ultimately naive drama. From the heart of Rome, and broadly in an Italian tradition of sentimentalist realism, film-maker Gianni Amelio brings us a fairytale…
body: There is some incidental interest and the film is beautifully shot, but finally it buckles under the weight of its own preposterousness and naivety. It is also sketchy about how and why people go into and come out of prison; the final shot, a supposedly heartwarming visionary moment of redemption and reconciliation, looks absurd.

Davide is a secondhand book dealer with a little-visited stall: who on earth reads books nowadays? He is played by Alessandro Borghi with something of that troubled decency that Peter Sarsgaard often projects. Evidently, Davide has got enough family money (and a handsome book-lined flat) that he doesn’t have to worry about sales. He flirts with a literature professor (Valeria Golino) but doesn’t quite have the maturity to pursue a relationship.

Davide’s world falls apart one day when he is approached in the street by a north African man (Ramzi Lafrindi) – perhaps a migrant or asylum seeker – hand-in-hand with a nine-year-old boy (Beidja Yahiaoui), whom he is clearly trying to be rid of. This man shoves the small boy into Davide’s arms, insisting that he is Davide’s responsibility.

articles.title: Pablo Torre Sounds Off on the NBA’s Historic Ruling Against the Clippers, Kawhi Leonard and ESPN — and Teases His Next Big Sports Investigation
articles.summary: Pablo Torre is feeling vindicated — sort of. Back in July, Variety spoke with the trailblazing sports journalist about “Pablo Torre Finds Out,” his engrossing podcast, a mélange of chat show and true-crime docuseries wherein Torre breadcrumbs investigative reporting to his pals, and its monthslong…
body: The NBA, who’d hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to conduct an independent investigation into the Clippers/Leonard saga, found that the Clippers had “committed multiple significant rules violations” and that Leonard, via his uncle, Dennis Robertson, had compelled the Clippers “to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses.”

Leonard released a statement saying, in part, “I accept full responsibility for the lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle,” while NBA commissioner Adam Silver said, “I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers’ institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations.” Ballmer, for his part, released his own statement accusing the NBA of “a heavily biased investigation” and adding they are “exploring every legal remedy to address this gross injustice.”

articles.title: ‘Marriagetoxin’ Creators Joumyaku and Yoda Mizuki Tease Season 2: ‘There Is Plenty of Cool Action We Want You to See’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: A master assassin’s toughest job isn’t a kill order. It’s finding a wife. That premise carried “Marriagetoxin” from a running Shonen Jump+ series into one of the standout anime of Spring 2026, and creators Joumyaku and Yoda Mizuki are already looking toward a second season set for January 2027.
body: The audience reaction has exceeded what either creator anticipated. Joumyaku points to Kinosaki’s reception specifically, crediting the anime staff for carrying Yoda’s character designs and action work faithfully into the adaptation. Yoda says they are grateful to the readers who have supported the series, to everyone involved in making it, and to Joumyaku for teaming up with them. “What surprises me most is that so many readers have enjoyed it – enough that Volume 1 went straight into a reprint and the dream of an adaptation came true.” Yoda says.

Both creators are already looking ahead to the second season. Joumyaku promises that even more captivating heroines will appear one after another, deepening the relationships surrounding Gero. “There is plenty of cool action we want you to see,” Joumyaku says, adding that they are very much looking forward to delivering it to fans. Yoda echoes that heading into Season 2, captivating new heroines arrive along with several characters they are fond of themselves.

articles.title: Wild Horse Nine review – Malkovich and Rockwell head to Easter Island for McDonagh’s acid bromance
articles.summary: Venice film festival Two men, some violence, much freewheeling chat: so far, so standard fare from the Oscar-winning writer-director. But this time the comedy and charm can feel diluted by blood and machismo.
body: I t isn’t a Martin McDonagh movie unless you’ve got two morose guys – one old, one not so old – who do nothing all the livelong day but bitch and snipe and quarrel and exchange barbed bromantic dialogue while occasionally going off on a plaintive tangent about nothing at all, incidentally revealing something very wrong with their friendship. If it can be called that. In The Banshees of Inisherin from 2022, the older guy decides he wants nothing more to do with the younger guy; in In Bruges from 14 years earlier (of which this latest film is almost a retread or maybe B-side), the older guy has an awful secret he is keeping from the younger guy.

articles.title: Beyoncé Releases ‘B’Day 20th Anniversary Deluxe Edition’ Featuring Unreleased Songs, Collaborations With Selena and Maluma
articles.summary: To commemorate the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album, Beyoncé has released a remastered version of “B’Day” featuring Spanish recordings, previously released bonus tracks, and a few unheard songs including “Can I Watch You” featuring Pharrell and a new Spanish version of “Irreplaceable”…
body: For the reissue, Beyoncé remastered the songs and videos, which were recolored and finished in 4k. The revamped visual for “Déjà Vu” featuring Jay-Z was also released alongside the album.

“B’Day 20th Anniversary Deluxe Edition” features a handful of unheard tracks, including “Cuerpo Tumbao (Get Me Bodied)” with Maluma, marking her first collaboration with the Colombian artist. The release notes that the song samples Celia Cruz’s “La Negra Tiene Tumbao” and that Beyoncé has “long admired Cruz’s pride in her African culture.” The song was produced by Beyoncé, Edgar Barrera, Casta and co-produced by Ali “Ali Ali” Alvarez.

Additionally, the reissue includes “Irreemplazable (Como La Flor)” featuring Selena Quintanilla, whose estate approved the duet. The release notes that Beyoncé “revered Selena,” a fellow Texan, “and remembers listening to her on the radio in Houston,” crediting the late singer for inspiring the recording of her 2007 Spanish EP “Irreemplazable.”

“B’Day 20th Anniversary Edition” also includes new and rare tracks including “Morning Dew (Donk),” “Can I Watch You” (produced by Beyoncé and Pharrell), “My First Time,” “Lost Yo Mind,” “Creole” and “Back Up.

articles.title: By Any Means review – Mark Wahlberg and Yahya Abdul-Mateen II drama provokes with horror of 1960s racism
articles.summary: Elegance Bratton’s civil rights drama in the Jim Crow south confronts you with almost unbearable brutality. Black people officially won the unrestricted right to vote in the US in 1965 but many still encountered hurdles on their path to the ballot box: 11 states in the south quickly introduced a…
body: It is Mississippi in the mid-60s and Wayne Strider (a sturdy Yahya Abdul-Mateen II ) is new to the local FBI unit, having recently moved back to his home state from Chicago, and is dealing with bosses who turn a blind eye to racist crimes. “White guys can get away with murder,” says one Black colleague while shaking his head. After his boss receives a message from President Johnson to prioritize the Dahmer murder case, Strider is teamed up with a widely feared mobster, Gregory Scarpa ( Mark Wahlberg with a rather distracting prosthetic nose), who has been shipped in from Brooklyn as part of an off-book mission to track down the Klansmen and bring justice to the killers.

Bratton aims to both expose and underline the racism that the US was built on by embellishing history with his own imagination. “I’m not interested in a prescriptive historical take,” the director said in a recent interview. “My film is not history. My film is using history in a way to comment on the contemporary condition.” The result is grimly effective while also being one of the most grisly and upsetting films in recent memory. As a provocation, By All Means is hard to forget.

articles.title: Girl group Katseye are missing two members, but their tour still dazzles
articles.summary: Reduced but resilient, girl group Katseye received a hero's welcome in London.
body: They may have been two members down, but the pop group Katseye received a hero's welcome as they played their first full concert in the UK.
The audience erupted with screams even before the show began, as the band broadcast their music videos on the O2 Arena's big screens, and the noise barely dipped for the next three hours.

It was proof that Katseye have become pop's biggest property (they're currently the most-streamed act on YouTube UK) even while singers Manon Bannerman and Sophia Laforteza are on health-related hiatus.
The stage felt emptier without them, but their bandmates worked hard to fill the gaps, hyping up the crowd with a succession of bass-heavy pop anthems and jaw-dropping dance breaks.

articles.title: Martin McDonagh says CIA has ‘done awful things all around the world’
articles.summary: McDonagh’s new film, Wild Horse Nine, stars John Malkovich as an agent in 1970s Chile who feels ‘guilt and regret’ over his role in global interventions. The US’s history of intervening in democratic processes around the world deserves more attention in the light of current political developments…
body: “I’ve been very interested in the truth of what the CIA has been doing over the last 60 years, and the awful things they’ve done all around the world,” McDonagh said about Wild Horse Nine, his first film since his 2022 tragicomedy The Banshees of Inisherin. “I think maybe something that’s not talked about enough. We know what the KGB are like, but we probably don’t question the CIA’s activity as much as we ought to.”

In Wild Horse Nine, John Malkovich plays Chris, a veteran agent for the foreign intelligence service who is stationed in Santiago, Chile, on the eve of the US-supported coup against Salvador Allende – Latin America’s first democratically elected Marxist president – in 1973. Recently diagnosed with cancer and acting erratically, Chris is dispatched to Easter Island with his protege Lee (Sam Rockwell), where he starts to reflect critically on his role in other CIA interventions, including the Guatemalan coup d’état of 1954, the 1961 assassination of revolutionary Congolese prime minister Patrice Lumumba and – according to the film’s telling – the killing of John F Kennedy.

articles.title: ‘Too Much Sugar’ Review: A Lively and Authentic Portrait of Small-Town America, in Which the Characters Become Masters of Their Own Stories
articles.summary: Robert Greene's latest hybrid feature mixes documentary and fiction to focus on a pair of 40-something friends from Missouri, exposing hardships they face as ex-cons and fathers.
body: Director and editor Robert Greene continues to intriguingly blur the lines between fact, fiction and filmmaking in his new hybrid feature, Too Much Sugar, which premiered in Venice ’s Orizzonti sidebar.

The two eventually became friends, and then collaborators, with Greene deciding to make a feature about Holliger, his sizable family and his best friend and fellow carpenter, Michael Midgyett, aka “AccRite.” You can see what the director found appealing about such a character: Raised by a single mom, the former convict spent four years in jail before becoming a manual laborer and amateur boxer. He now dedicates his life to being the best father possible — no easy task when taking into account that he has six children from five different mothers.

Per his own words, Holliger excels at “making bad decisions that turn into great kids,” and such energy and positivity seem to rub off on his many offspring, who range from ages 8 to 24 and whom Holliger coaches through various sports (basketball, baseball, boxing and soccer) while also housing and feeding most of them with the help of his current partner, Amanda.

articles.title: Jive Bunny And The Mastermixers creator dies at 84
articles.summary: Tributes are paid to John Pickles, who formed the novelty pop act in Rotherham in 1989.
body: The man behind the novelty pop act Jive Bunny and The Mastermixers has died aged 84, the company he founded has confirmed.
John Pickles formed Jive Bunny in Rotherham in 1989 and the act went on to have three UK number ones with Swing The Mood, That's What I Like and Let's Party.
Jive Bunny records typically used synthesisers and sampling to combine contemporary pop music with hits from the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.

A statement from the Mastermix company described Pickles as "a true pioneer in the music industry", adding that he was "a leader, an entrepreneur, a businessman and an incredibly talented songwriter".
